---
title: "Setup"
---

This is the shortest path from a fresh clone to a rendered table.

## Prerequisites

- **Python 3.10+**. `great_tables` and the harness both require it.
- **Node.js 20+** — the Claude Agent SDK depends on the Claude Code CLI,
  which is a Node package.
- **An Anthropic API key** with credits — the harness calls the API
  once per prompt per repeat, plus once per judge invocation. Cost
  scales with `--model` (see [runner reference](runner.qmd#-model-label_or_id--defaults-haiku)).
- **macOS or Linux.** The sidecar-Chrome/CDP path in
  [`runner/sidecar.py`](https://github.com/HrudithL/gt-skill/blob/main/runner/sidecar.py)
  is exercised on macOS; Linux is expected to work with a
  distribution-provided Chromium.

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/HrudithL/gt-skill
cd gt-skill

# 1) Python environment
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install claude-agent-sdk great_tables pandas python-dotenv anyio pillow
pip install anthropic     # for the ground-truth judge (runner/judge.py)
pip install plotnine      # for regenerating the eval-results plots

# 2) Claude Code CLI (the SDK shells out to it)
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```

::: {.callout-note}
## No extras for the UI
The old browser-based control plane is gone. The Quarto site you're
reading right now is the only "UI" — everything else runs from the
CLI. If your workflow was `uvicorn web.server:app`, use `python
run.py --flags` instead. See the [runner reference](runner.qmd) for
every flag.
:::

## API key

Create a `.env` at the repo root:

```
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
```

`run.py` reads it via `python-dotenv` before doing anything else. If
the variable is missing the runner exits with code `2` and a clear
error — no half-run partial artifacts.

Optional overrides (usually you don't set these by hand):

```
GTSKILL_JUDGE_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5   # override the judge model
GTSKILL_AGENT_MODEL=claude-haiku-4-5  # set from --model; setting here overrides
```

See the [environment variables table](runner.qmd#environment-variables)
for the full list.

## Sample data

`data/` is gitignored so a fresh clone has no CSVs. One command
materializes every dataset the harness uses:

```bash
python scripts/fetch_data.py
```

The script reads pandas DataFrames from `great_tables.data` (the
sample datasets the Great Tables package ships for its own examples)
and writes one CSV per dataset into `data/`. It is idempotent —
re-running is a no-op unless you pass `--force`. Use `--list` to see
which datasets would be written without touching disk.

```bash
python scripts/fetch_data.py --list      # print dataset names, exit
python scripts/fetch_data.py             # write missing CSVs
python scripts/fetch_data.py --force     # overwrite existing CSVs
```

## Verifying the install

The smallest possible end-to-end check:

```bash
python run.py --skill prose \
              --prompt-text "Top 10 cars by MSRP with country of origin" \
              --data data/gtcars.csv
```

Expected output:

- A new directory under `runs/single/<timestamp>_prose_adhoc/`.
- `runs/.../prompts/adhoc/repeat_1/table.png` — the rendered table.
- Exit code `0`.

If Chrome fails to launch (e.g. wrong architecture), the sidecar log
in the run directory shows why. If the API call fails, the runner
surfaces the SDK's error and exits `1` — no silent retry.

Once that works, you're ready for the [reproduction guide](reproduce.qmd).
